title: Mizraim
summary: Son of Ham (Gen 10:6); the Hebrew name of Egypt. Ussher (Second Age §51, 2188 BC) and CFAH (Menes = Mizraim) date his colony in Egypt to 2188 BC; see the Egyptian-cities event.
description: Son of Ham (Gen 10:6); the Hebrew name of Egypt. Ussher (Second Age §51, 2188 BC) and CFAH (Menes = Mizraim) date his colony in Egypt to 2188 BC; see the Egyptian-cities event. Josephus (Antiquities I.6.2, Whiston): "all we who inhabit this country [of Judea] called Egypt Mestre, and the Egyptians Mestreans"

sorting_basis.note: PROVISIONAL: no CFAH, Ussher–Jones or Ussher date exists, so the sort uses Generations (Taking Africa for Jesus, PDF p. 19): around 2478 BC. Pending owner decision (open question A8).

birth.note: pending CFAH reference. CFAH dates the Table-of-Nations framework (first territorial division AP-27, 2254 BC; final division AP-28, 2247 BC; Dispersion AP-2, 2192/2191 BC) but not this individual birth

No birth year. Ussher Second Age §51 (1816d AM, 2188 BC) records Mizraim leading his colony into Egypt; see egyptian-cities-founded.

birth.note: Jordan: "If we assume births every two years, and about 30 years between generations ... we can come up with an approximate series of dates" (hypothetical, not stated by Scripture).

reign.date: arrived there, it is thought, about the fifteenth year of Nimrod, A. M. 1772
reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 183 (facsimile PDF p. 279)
reign.note: Mizraim’s arrival in Egypt. Page 186 repeats A. M. 1772 as the Hebrew beginning of Menes’ reign. Page 187 also prints A. M. 1805 and does not choose. See open question K5.

reign.date: Menes beginning his reign, as we said before, A. M. 1772
reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 186 (facsimile PDF p. 282)
reign.note: He calls this the Hebrew chronology, and he identifies Menes with Mizraim. The same sentence dates Sesac’s siege at A. M. 3033.

reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 187 (facsimile PDF p. 283)
reign.note: A second computation of Menes’ first year, nine hundred and eighty-seven years before Nilus. He writes that he cannot say which of A. M. 1772 and A. M. 1805, or whether either, is the exact truth. See open question K5.

reign.date: one hundred and twenty-four years after the dispersion of mankind, i. e. A. M. 1881
reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 187 (facsimile PDF p. 283)
reign.note: Apollodorus, as Shuckford reports him, for Menes’ removal into Thebais. Not a second start of the reign.
